Dear participants,

We have prepared a more challenging experimental dataset of 100 Order-5 Hard problems involving Austin laws. For each problem, at least one of Eq1 or Eq2 is an Austin law. The ground truth for some of these problems is currently unknown.

Experimental dataset:
https://huggingface.co/datasets/SAIRfoundation/equational-theories-selected-problems/viewer/research_order5_hard

For more background on Order-5 Austin laws, see the Equational Theories blueprint:
https://teorth.github.io/equational_theories/blueprint/order-5-austin-laws.html

These problems are intended only for experimentation and research. They will not be included in the main leaderboard evaluation.

Thank you for your participation and support!

I took up the challenge for research_order5_hard_0014:

Eq1 = 40909 → Eq2 = 28770.

After working through Eq. 40909, I now have a Lean kernel-checked countermodel, so the implication is:

Equation 40909⇏Equation 28770\boxed{\mathrm{Equation}\ 40909 \not\Rightarrow \mathrm{Equation}\ 28770}Equation 40909⇒Equation 28770​

In other words, problem 0014 is FALSE.

There are a few structural facts about Eq. 40909 that may be worth recording, because the result turned out to be stronger than just deciding this implication.

Eq. 40909 is

((((y⋄x)⋄y)⋄y)⋄z)⋄y=x.((((y \diamond x)\diamond y)\diamond y)\diamond z)\diamond y=x.((((y⋄x)⋄y)⋄y)⋄z)⋄y=x.

For fixed yyy, Eq. 40909 implies left cancellation:

y⋄a=y⋄b⟹a=b.y\diamond a=y\diamond b \quad\Longrightarrow\quad a=b.y⋄a=y⋄b⟹a=b.

Every right translation is also surjective.

More importantly, define

Φy(x,z)=(((y⋄x)⋄y)⋄y)⋄z.\Phi_y(x,z)=(((y\diamond x)\diamond y)\diamond y)\diamond z.Φy​(x,z)=(((y⋄x)⋄y)⋄y)⋄z.

Then Eq. 40909 gives

Φy(x,z)⋄y=x,\Phi_y(x,z)\diamond y=x,Φy​(x,z)⋄y=x,

and one obtains an injection

Φy:G×G↪G.\Phi_y:G\times G\hookrightarrow G.Φy​:G×G↪G.

Therefore every finite nonempty model of Eq. 40909 is trivial.

Another useful consequence is that an idempotent collapses the entire model:

y⋄y=y⟹∀a,b, a=b.y\diamond y=y \quad\Longrightarrow\quad \forall a,b,\ a=b.y⋄y=y⟹∀a,b, a=b.

This gives a particularly short connection with Eq. 28770.

Under Eq. 40909, the diagonal instance of Eq. 28770 obtained by taking x=yx=yx=y and z=yz=yz=y forces

y⋄y=y.y\diamond y=y.y⋄y=y.

Hence, among models of Eq. 40909,

Eq28770⟺the model is trivial.\mathrm{Eq28770} \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \text{the model is trivial}.Eq28770⟺the model is trivial.

So the original implication reduces to the real question:

Does Eq. 40909 admit a nontrivial model?

The answer is yes.

The construction came from an infinite recursive rewrite forest.

Orient Eq. 40909 as the initial rule

R0:((((y⋄x)⋄y)⋄y)⋄z)⋄y  ⟶  x.R_0:\qquad ((((y\diamond x)\diamond y)\diamond y)\diamond z)\diamond y \;\longrightarrow\;x.R0​:((((y⋄x)⋄y)⋄y)⋄z)⋄y⟶x.

Suppose a branch has the form

A⋄p⟶q.A\diamond p\longrightarrow q.A⋄p⟶q.

Eq. 40909 generates the next branch

((((q⋄A)⋄A)⋄z)⋄A)  ⟶  p.((((q\diamond A)\diamond A)\diamond z)\diamond A) \;\longrightarrow\;p.((((q⋄A)⋄A)⋄z)⋄A)⟶p.

Iterating this produces an infinite family

R0,R1,R2,…R_0,R_1,R_2,\ldotsR0​,R1​,R2​,…

with a very rigid recursive structure.

During completion, the branch interactions exhibited the pattern

Ri⋈Rj  ⇝  Ri+j+1.R_i\bowtie R_j \;\leadsto\; R_{i+j+1}.Ri​⋈Rj​⇝Ri+j+1​.

This led to a forest formulation with a trunk, recursive branches, promotion, provenance, rank, and normal leaves.

The final proof does not depend on checking only finitely many critical pairs.

Instead, I construct the magma of hereditarily normal terms.

For two normal terms a,ba,ba,b, their product is defined by:

  • reducing a⋄ba\diamond ba⋄b if it is a root instance of one of the recursive rules RnR_nRn​;
  • otherwise retaining the raw node a⋄ba\diamond ba⋄b.

The main structural facts are then proved:

  1. root reduction is functional;
  2. every recursive rule strictly decreases term size;
  3. variables are irreducible normal leaves;
  4. the normal-term magma satisfies Eq. 40909;
  5. two distinct variables remain distinct.

A canonical normalization map nf\mathrm{nf}nf is then defined.

Every rewrite step preserves this normal form, and every term rewrites to its canonical normal form. Hence every local fork joins.

This gives the full local-join theorem

LocalForestJoin,\mathrm{LocalForestJoin},LocalForestJoin,

and global confluence follows from strict descent together with a measure-based Newman argument.

The final Lean certificate proves

∃G,G⊨Eq40909∧G⊭Eq28770.\exists G,\qquad G\models \mathrm{Eq40909} \quad\land\quad G\not\models \mathrm{Eq28770}.∃G,G⊨Eq40909∧G⊨Eq28770.

So the final result is

Eq40909⇏Eq28770.\boxed{\mathrm{Eq40909}\not\Rightarrow\mathrm{Eq28770}.}Eq40909⇒Eq28770.​

There is also a stronger consequence.

Since every finite nonempty model of Eq. 40909 is trivial, while the constructed model is nontrivial, this model must be infinite.

Therefore Eq. 40909 itself admits a nontrivial infinite model.

So Eq. 40909 is an Austin law as well.

Eq. 28770 was already a known Austin law; thus problem 0014 gives an interesting situation where both sides are Austin laws, but the implication still fails.

The complete final Lean kernel check finished with:

EXIT_CODE=0

on my machine.

The final verification run took approximately 8m27s. The research and discovery process was, of course, substantially longer.

I would be very interested if someone wants to independently inspect the recursive RnR_nRn​ construction, the normal-term magma, or the forest-completion argument.

Now that 0014 is settled:

which one would you like me to look at next? :smile:

I genuinely love this research dataset.

A few details on how I solved E11116, since the final FALSE certificates hide most of the actual construction.

The source law is

E11116:y⋄((x⋄(z⋄x))⋄(y⋄y))=x.\mathrm{E11116}:\qquad y\diamond\bigl((x\diamond(z\diamond x))\diamond(y\diamond y)\bigr)=x.E11116:y⋄((x⋄(z⋄x))⋄(y⋄y))=x.

The countermodel is not obtained from a small finite search.

The construction uses an infinite recursive rewrite forest on the free term algebra.

The initial node is

A0=y,p0=(x⋄(z⋄x))⋄(y⋄y),q0=x,A_0=y, \qquad p_0=(x\diamond(z\diamond x))\diamond(y\diamond y), \qquad q_0=x,A0​=y,p0​=(x⋄(z⋄x))⋄(y⋄y),q0​=x,

so that

A0⋄p0⟶q0A_0\diamond p_0\longrightarrow q_0A0​⋄p0​⟶q0​

is exactly an oriented instance of E11116.

The important point is that this rule cannot simply be used in isolation.

The structural overlaps force the construction of an infinite recursive family.

From a node

(An,pn,qn)(A_n,p_n,q_n)(An​,pn​,qn​)

the next node is generated by introducing a fresh variable:

An+1=vn+3,A_{n+1}=v_{n+3},An+1​=vn+3​,

pn+1=(pn⋄qn)⋄(vn+3⋄vn+3),p_{n+1} = (p_n\diamond q_n)\diamond (v_{n+3}\diamond v_{n+3}),pn+1​=(pn​⋄qn​)⋄(vn+3​⋄vn+3​),

qn+1=pn.q_{n+1}=p_n.qn+1​=pn​.

Hence we obtain an infinite family of root reductions

An⋄pn⟶qn,n=0,1,2,…A_n\diamond p_n\longrightarrow q_n, \qquad n=0,1,2,\ldotsAn​⋄pn​⟶qn​,n=0,1,2,…

The real difficulty is then to prove that this infinite family defines a coherent magma rather than an ambiguous rewrite system.

The Lean development formalizes:

  • the free term algebra;
  • substitution;
  • subterms and strict subterms;
  • a natural size measure;
  • preservation of subterm relations under substitution;
  • strict decrease of generated reductions;
  • contextual rewriting;
  • root-shape classification;
  • uniqueness of root outputs;
  • normal forms;
  • preservation of normality by the final operation.

A central invariant is

qn is a strict subterm of pn.q_n\ \text{is a strict subterm of}\ p_n.qn​ is a strict subterm of pn​.

Therefore

∣qn∣<∣pn∣,|q_n|<|p_n|,∣qn​∣<∣pn​∣,

and this remains true after arbitrary substitution:

∣σ(qn)∣<∣σ(pn)∣.|\sigma(q_n)|<|\sigma(p_n)|.∣σ(qn​)∣<∣σ(pn​)∣.

This gives strict descent for every generated root rule.

Another essential theorem is root functionality:

R(s,t)∧R(s,u)⟹t=u.R(s,t)\land R(s,u) \Longrightarrow t=u.R(s,t)∧R(s,u)⟹t=u.

So even though the root family is infinite, a term can never reduce at the root to two different outputs.

A substantial part of the proof is devoted to showing that dangerous shapes cannot accidentally become roots.

For example, the development proves exclusion results for configurations such as

a⋄a,a\diamond a,a⋄a,

a⋄vk,a\diamond v_k,a⋄vk​,

a⋄(b⋄vk),a\diamond(b\diamond v_k),a⋄(b⋄vk​),

together with further exclusions coming from size inequalities and recursive shape constraints.

These exclusion theorems are crucial: they make it possible to know exactly when multiplication performs a reduction and when it simply constructs a new normal term.

The key recursive result is the promotion theorem.

Suppose

z⋄x⟶q.z\diamond x\longrightarrow q.z⋄x⟶q.

Then the recursive forest contains the higher-level rule required to force

y⋄((x⋄q)⋄(y⋄y))⟶x.y\diamond \bigl((x\diamond q)\diamond(y\diamond y)\bigr) \longrightarrow x.y⋄((x⋄q)⋄(y⋄y))⟶x.

For E11116, one can organize the model around a rigid recursive root family and prove functionality plus normality.
